Keep that unit physically exactly in its existing position. It must be VACANT: simple empty interior visible through glass, no seated customers or occupied terrace tables belonging to this unit. Existing neighboring cafes on both sides remain busy with occupied tables. Pedestrians walk continuously along the shared front pavement. Emphasize only this FRONT blue awning with stronger blue. Put a small accurate annotation 'Sid’s proposed café' with a leader line directly pointing to this foreground blue-awning unit.
The detached single-storey central shop across the road is now just a neutral LOCAL SHOP, not Sid's site. Preserve that building and its existing parking geometry, but use a pale gray plain awning instead of strong blue stripes and remove ALL proposed-cafe annotation pointing at it. Remove old dashed blue 'Opening view' boundary surrounding central building. If any opening view guide appears, it must instead enclose ONLY the foreground cafe ROW, showing Sid's vacant unit surrounded by busy neighboring cafes; no guide needed if cluttered.
Keep tall residential towers back LEFT; office buildings upper RIGHT; underground metro middle RIGHT beside the busy intersection; all road connections, skyline and planted areas unchanged. Rough graphite sketch with construction lines and very light pale blue wash, white paper. Not a polished render. Keep whole map framed. No extra panels, no demographic claims, no invented outcome. storyboard_prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Create an UPDATED FIVE-CLICK ROUGH STORYBOARD, correcting Sid's location to a vacant storefront IN THE FOREGROUND ROW OF EXISTING CAFES, not across the street.
Reference image 1 is the updated neighborhood geography and spatial authority. Sid's proposed unit is the TWO-STOREY vivid BLUE-AWNING storefront in the BOTTOM FOREGROUND ROW, with operating beige-awning cafes on its left and orange-awning cafe on its right. The neutral single-storey shop at CENTER across the road is ONLY A LOCAL SHOP. Never identify or highlight that central shop as Sid's cafe. Do not relocate buildings. Apartment towers back left, offices upper right, underground metro middle right, competing cafe row bottom, shared parking at right end of that foreground row.

Important correction to reference image: remove any tables, seats, parasols and seated customers directly in front of Sid's blue-awning vacant unit. Its glass windows must reveal a bare unfitted interior with no counter, tables or cafe patrons. A small 'TO LET' notice on glass makes vacancy clear. Pedestrians may walk along its pavement. Neighboring cafes remain busy, with their own seated customers and outdoor tables on their own frontages. This visual difference is essential. Preserve the whole neighborhood, only correct that unit's occupancy. Keep Sid's unit in this SAME ROW in all five frames, never opening successfully or moving to another site.

Portrait review sheet, five horizontal rows. Left 60% per row pencil sketch; right 40% clean legible copy on white, tiny numbered title and small camera note. Rough graphite, sparse facade marks, light pale-blue wash, rough tree masses, small gestural people, not polished 3D. Title verbatim 'GEOMARKETEER — A SPOT IN THE CAFÉ LANE'. Subtitle 'Five clicks. One neighborhood. One decision.'

ROW 01 — THE IDEA
Sketch: VERY TIGHT zoom into the BOTTOM FRONT CAFE LANE ONLY. Four adjoining storefronts with Sid's empty BLUE-AWNING two-storey unit near middle, existing busy cafes immediately either side. Camera closer than the full reference; facade, tables, shared pavement and people fill panel. No central detached shop, no metro, no offices, no towers in this shot.
Headline: 'Sid wanted a café of his own.'
Support: 'This busy café lane looked like a promising place.'
Small camera note: 'Open close on the front lane, not the whole map.'

ROW 02 — THE ASSUMPTION
Sketch: still tightly within that SAME foreground cafe row. Focus closer on the vacant blue-awning unit and its busy cafe neighbors on both sides. Blue leader line points at the EMPTY unit, small label 'Sid’s proposed unit'. Window has 'TO LET' notice. Do not show central detached shop, metro or skyline.
Headline: 'The cafés next door were busy.'
Support: 'Surely there was room for one more?'
Small camera note: 'Highlight the vacant unit within the existing café row.'

ROW 03 — THE DOUBT
Sketch: widen RIGHTWARD and back from the front row, keeping Sid's same blue-awning unit visible near lower left and revealing the shared parking at row's right end, crossing and busy sidewalk that leads to the metro stairwell further back on RIGHT. Some commuters walk along pavement. Residential and office skyline outside crop or only faint clipped edges. Central detached shop may enter periphery as neutral gray, never highlighted. Metro visible for FIRST time here.
Headline: 'But what was bringing people here?'
Support: 'The metro explained some of the crowd. It didn’t tell Sid who would buy.'
Small camera note: 'Pull back to reveal the metro and pedestrian routes.'

ROW 04 — THE CONTEXT
Sketch: FULL wide neighborhood exactly matching reference 1, not a remixed map. Tall residential society back LEFT, offices top RIGHT, metro mid RIGHT, neutral local shop at CENTER, Sid's BLUE-AWNING EMPTY UNIT in FRONT CAFE ROW at BOTTOM. Three tiny area-level labels around map: 'People', 'Spending', 'Competition'. Use subtle area annotations rather than attaching income to office or age to individuals. No measured values.
Headline: 'He needed more than footfall.'
Support: 'Who lives and works nearby? What do they spend? What do the existing cafés already offer?'
Small camera note: 'Reveal the wider neighborhood around the same café lane.'

ROW 05 — THE RESPONSE
Sketch: SAME FULL MAP, quieter context drawing, small blue marker anchored ONLY to the BOTTOM-ROW BLUE-AWNING VACANT UNIT. Keep towers, offices, metro, central neutral shop, cafe row and parking in identical positions. No relocation, no successful cafe launch, no recommended different property. Optional subtle labels 'People · Spending · Competition'.
Headline: 'Same lane. A clearer picture.'
Support: 'GeoMarketeer helps businesses understand a neighborhood before choosing where to open.'
Role line: 'My role: UX Research & Interaction Design'
Small camera note: 'End the story. Optional exploration follows.'

All text above should be typeset cleanly, readable and verbatim. Exactly five rows, clear camera progression. No large Sid cartoon, no thought bubbles, no floating UI cards, no demographic values, no proven-demand or success claims. The first two frames MUST be zoomed into ONLY the front cafe lane. The proposed unit is EMPTY and WITHIN that row, never the detached center shop.
